narrative.overview:
The site reads like a working scientist's notebook made public. Every page states a finding in the largest type it can hold, then shows the measurement underneath: the number, what it was measured against, whether it is significant. The one colour that is not ink is a highlighter, used the way a person marks the line they want read again, and it never stands for data.

The voice is confident and plain. Headlines state findings ("Small models lead, largely on disputed labels."), text underneath is quiet and grey, and nothing decorative appears unless it carries meaning: the faint grid behind the hero is graph paper, the glow is the highlighter's bleed. It is dark-first, on near-black, with a warm-paper light theme that keeps every role.

- Very large, tightly set display headlines (800 weight, -0.035em), usually one clause turned in Highlighter Lime. - Monospace for every label, kicker, eyebrow, navigation link and number; a humanist sans for reading. - Flat surfaces separated by hairlines and a single tone step, never by shadow. - Three categorical colours for the kinds of model, kept apart from the accent. - No web fonts, and no external request but the cookieless analytics PRODUCT.md names: the type falls back to the system's sans and mono.

rules.name: The Highlighter Rule
rules.body: The accent marks what to read; it never encodes a value. A chart never uses it for a series, and a table never uses it for a number.

rules.name: The Three Kinds Rule
rules.body: Blue, ember and green always mean proprietary, local and open weights, wherever they appear, and nothing else.

rules.name: The Mono Means Exact Rule
rules.body: Anything a reader might copy, count or click to navigate is set in monospace: commands, ids, numbers, labels, links in the bar. Prose never is.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: A card, a chart and a table sit on the page with a hairline. A shadow means the element floats above the page and will close.

dos: **Do** state the finding in the headline and turn one clause of it in Highlighter Lime.
**Do** set every label, number, command and id in monospace with tabular figures.
**Do** separate surfaces with a 1px hairline and one tone step.
**Do** keep blue, ember and green for proprietary, local and open-weights arms only.
**Do** keep both themes complete: every colour is a token defined for dark and light.
donts: **Don't** use the lime accent for a data series, a value or a status.
**Don't** add a shadow to a card, a chart or a table; only a floating panel has one.
**Don't** load a web font or any other external resource (the cookieless analytics excepted).
**Don't** add decoration that carries no meaning: the grid is graph paper, the glow is the highlighter.
